title: Terraform SemVer Decision Tree + Release Bulletin (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft: a concise decision tree and accompanying customer-facing release bulletin template for Terraform module releases used by Private (VPC/on-prem) customers. Goal is to reduce risky breaking updates, standardize semver decisions, and speed up safe publication to the internal registry.

Scope:
- Applies to all terraform modules maintained under terraform-modules/* that are published to the private registry used in on-prem deployments.
- Focus on: API contract changes (inputs/outputs), resource refactors, and provider constraints that could cause customer infra drift or failed applies.
- NOT covering: docs-only changes, CI test infra updates, or readme fixes (those are patch-level and handled by normal PR process).

Quick decision tree (high level):
1) Change discovery: Dev opens PR and fills the "module-change-report" checklist in PR template. CI runs sanity tests.
2) Categorize change type:
   - Typo/docs-only / formatting: PATCH -> no registry version bump required unless release requested.
   - Non-functional refactor (no schema change): PATCH -> minor internal tag OK, run compatibility test.
   - Backwards-compatible new input with default: MINOR -> publish new minor version, set deprecation warnings if behavior may change at scale.
   - Input default changed OR input made required OR input type changed: MAJOR -> requires migration plan, deprecation window, and coordinated release committee sign-off.
   - Output removed OR output type changed: MAJOR -> treat as breaking.
   - Resource address rename that breaks state (resource name or type change): MAJOR unless alias shim is provided.
   - Provider upgrade that changes resource semantics (e.g., provider v3->v4 with breaking changes): evaluate on a module-by-module basis; often MAJOR.

Decision criteria matrix (examples):
- PATCH (no registry bump): README tweak, comments, metadata, CI-only tooling.
- PATCH (registry patch): bugfix that does not change module interface but backports behavior safe for existing consumers (rare).
- MINOR: Add optional variable with sane default, add new output, add new resource behind a flag.
- MAJOR: Change variable name, remove output, make optional->required, change type, rename resource addresses without aliases, remove support for an edge-case provider.

Required pre-release checks (always run):
- Unit tests (local terraform validate + module unit harness).
- Integration apply-to-drift tests against a cached test cluster (use minimal infra with recorded state).
- State-migration smoke test if resource renames/aliases proposed.
- Automated lint (tflint + custom rules), semantic PR title enforcement.
- Manual review: peer + module owner.

Additional gating for MAJOR decisions:
- Fill migration plan template (see 'Migration plan' section below).
- Schedule canary in staging and one small customer-config test (if consented).
- Create Jira ticket with customer-impact tag and set SLA for response if customers report issues.
- Release window must be coordinated with Solutions/Support for on-prem customers.

Migration plan (minimum fields):
- Change summary (one sentence).
- Why breaking (technical explanation).
- Detection (how to identify consumers that will break: Terraform state patterns, provider versions).
- Migration steps (exact terraform state commands, aliasing examples, codemod snippet).
- Rollback steps (exact version pin and expected outcome).
- Customer-facing notes (short paragraph to paste into release bulletin).

Release checklist (publish runbook):
- [ ] PR merged to main with semver tag in title (e.g. v1.2.0 -> minor).
- [ ] Tag release in git and include changelog entry.
- [ ] CI: release pipeline creates package and runs publish dry-run.
- [ ] Registry publish: push to private registry staging bucket.
- [ ] Snapshot compatibility tests run against staging registry.
- [ ] Canary promotion: select one internal team or consenting customer for early rollout.
- [ ] Monitor canary for 72 hours: errors, diffs in 'terraform plan', state drift.
- [ ] Final promotion to stable and broadcast release bulletin.

Rollback & mitigation playbook (short):
- If a breaking failure is detected in canary: revert registry pointer to previous version, open incident channel with tag #tf-release-incident, page module owner.
- If customers in the wild are impacted and cannot upgrade/downgrade: provide targeted patch (patch-level fix) OR provide a compatibility shim (alias resource + outputs) and publish as new minor/patch.

Automation suggestions (TODOs for infra):
- CI job that auto-classifies PR diffs (variable changes, output changes, resource rename) and suggests semver bump.
- Codemod scripts to add alias blocks automatically when resource names change (examples for aws_ -> aws_renamed).
- Registry publish dry-run report emailed to module owners listing possible consumers impacted (based on dependency graph).

Customer-facing release bulletin (template — fill for each release):
- Subject: [Module] <module-name> vX.Y.Z published — impact summary
- Short summary (2 lines): What changed and why.
- Who this affects: e.g., "If you pin module >= v1.3.0 in your terraform.lock or module source with version constraint, you will not be affected unless you explicitly upgrade."
- Upgrade notes: step-by-step instructions for upgrading or pinning. Include explicit terraform commands for state migration if required.
- Rollback instructions: pin to previous version and run `terraform init -upgrade=false` + `terraform plan` to validate.
- Contact & support: link to support runbook, Jira template for reporting regression, scheduled office hours for the week following GA.

Example bulletin (MAJOR change):
- Subject: aws-networking v2.0.0 published — variable rename + output removal
- Summary: v2.0.0 renames variable `vpc_id` -> `network_id` and removes output `public_subnet_ids`. This was done to align naming with cross-module standards and to collapse two outputs for clearer state.
- Who this affects: Any on-prem deployment that references `module.aws-networking.public_subnet_ids` or passes `vpc_id` explicitly.
- Upgrade notes:
  1) If you do not upgrade, nothing changes.
  2) To upgrade, run `terraform init -upgrade` on an environment copy and follow the migration steps in the migration plan (alias-based resource rename provided in v2.0.0 to preserve state in 95% cases).
  3) If alias fails, follow the explicit state mv commands listed in the migration plan.
- Support: open INF-XXXX ticket with module=aws-networking, severity, and attach `terraform plan` output.

Communications & timing guidance:
- Draft bulletin at least 5 business days before promotion to stable for MINOR/MAJOR.
- For MAJOR, broadcast to customer success and on-call SRE with 48h runway.
- Post-release: 1-week status update in #tf-updates channel and update Confluence changelog.

Notes to self / unresolved items:
- Decide whether provider version bumps that are purely bugfix (e.g., provider 3.7.1 -> 3.7.2) should auto-pass as patch or be flagged when they touch resources used by module.
- Need a reliable way to enumerate registry consumers internally (build query on module lockfiles or published stacks).
- Ask legal about wording for forced migrations to avoid liability language.
- Add checklist item: verify KMS/HSM integration tests for private-deploy modules that touch encryption resources.

Appendix: small examples
- Example: Making var "enable_logging" default from false -> true (behavior change): classify as MINOR if callers rely on default=false? If existing users expect false, changing default is a MAJOR if it can create new resources or change security posture. We default to MAJOR for default flips that affect resource creation.
- Example: Adding `tags` output: MINOR.
- Example: Renaming resource `aws_lb_listener` -> `aws_alb_listener` with alias provided: MINOR if alias covers state; otherwise MAJOR.

PR template checklist (to include in repo):
* [ ] Change type described (patch/minor/major) and justification
* [ ] Migration plan attached if required
* [ ] Unit/integration tests included or updated
* [ ] Lint & formatting passed
* [ ] Module owner sign-off

— end of draft —

Action items after review:
- Carlos: mock up CI auto-classifier by end of Q3 (WIP).
- Aisha: draft a short Confluence how-to for migration plan examples.
- Maya: convert this doc into the release template page and add to release checklist repo.
